scenes.text: A viral chart says no open model since August uses full attention in every layer. Is that true?
scenes.say: A chart going round says no open model since late August uses full attention in every layer. Is that true?

scenes.headline: How open LLMs are trading full attention away
scenes.sub: A viral chart, recounted from the configs
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Vesna! I read the config file of every model on the chart's list, and many more. Let's count layers.

scenes.title: The chart and its source
scenes.sub: Three bars, and a gallery behind them
scenes.say: Chapter one. The chart and its source.

steps.say: Here is the chart as posted. The drawings carry Sebastian Raschka's watermark.
Most models were full attention throughout in twenty twenty-five, about a quarter early this year, and none since late August. The counts match Raschka's architecture gallery.

scenes.title: The gallery, reclassified from configs
scenes.note: share with full attention in every layer
scenes.say: I classified every layer of every gallery model from its config. The three bars come out exactly. The chart is an honest picture of the gallery.

scenes.title: What counts as full
scenes.sub: Six kinds of layer, and one convention
scenes.say: Chapter two. What counts as full attention?

scenes.title: Which earlier tokens a query reads

steps.label: full attention
steps.term: Full attention: every token reads every earlier token
steps.say: Full attention: every new token scores every earlier key. Grouped query and latent attention still count. They shrink each entry, but keep one per token.

steps.label: sliding window
steps.say: A window layer reads only the last few tokens.

steps.label: index-selected sparse
steps.term: Indexer: a small scorer that picks the top tokens
steps.say: A sparse layer lets an indexer pick the top few, and attention reads only those. It can still reach any token, but the chart counts it as not full.

scenes.title: What one layer keeps, per token
scenes.text: KV bytes per token = 2 x h_kv x d x b
scenes.say: Here is what a full layer costs.

parts.say: Two, for a key and a value.
Times the number of key value heads.
Times the width of each head.
Times the bytes per number. And every token of context adds that again, in every full layer.

scenes.title: Five layer stacks, one cell per layer

steps.say: Here is the census as strips, one cell per layer. K2 Horizon, from this autumn: every layer is plain full attention.
Gemma four: five window layers, then one full layer, over and over.

steps.term: Gated DeltaNet: the past folded into a fixed state
steps.say: Qwen three point eight: three linear layers that fold the past into a fixed state, then one full layer.
Kimi K three, the chart's own example: the same pattern, with Kimi Delta Attention as the linear layer.
K three point one Pro keeps every tensor, but its twenty-four full layers gained an indexer. They are still there. They stopped counting as full.
MiniMax M three had three full layers. M three point one Flash made them sparse too. Same backbone, new class.

scenes.title: A wider list
scenes.sub: The gallery is curated. Open models are not.

scenes.title: Full attention in every layer, by window

steps.say: The gallery draws architectures worth drawing. So I added sixty-five open releases from this site's coverage, and dropped fine-tunes that reuse another model's layers.
The first two windows barely move. The last one does: fourteen point three percent, not zero.
The decline is real. The zero belongs to the list.

scenes.label: Releases since 26 August with full attention in every layer
scenes.say: Five of thirty-five: three K2 Horizon models, Nanbeige and MiniCPM. Mostly small. By parameters, full attention is nearly gone.

scenes.quote: 0% used full attention throughout; 48% used no full-attention layers.
scenes.say: The second half of the claim needs a closer look. What is in that last bar?

scenes.title: No full is not no global
scenes.sub: What the last bar is made of
scenes.say: Chapter four. No full attention is not no global attention.

steps.say: Every no full attention model since August keeps a layer like this. The query meets a small index key for every earlier token.
The indexer keeps the best few hundred to two thousand tokens or blocks.
Attention reads only those. But the whole cache is kept, because any token might be picked next.
So sparse layers cut what each step reads, not what the server stores. All eleven such models can still reach every earlier token.
Kimi K three's own diagram: three delta layers, then one latent attention layer. Add an indexer to those, and the chart calls it no full attention.

scenes.title: What it buys, what it costs
scenes.sub: Memory at long context, and retrieval
scenes.say: Chapter five. What it buys, and what it costs.

steps.say: One full layer of Qwen three point eight keeps four thousand and ninety-six bytes per token.
Sixteen of them: sixty-four kibibytes.
At its full context, seventeen point two gigabytes for one sequence.
All full, it would be sixty-eight point seven.
The other forty-eight layers hold a fixed state of a hundred and forty-four mebibytes, at any length.

scenes.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash at 1M tokens
scenes.note: one sequence, BF16 cache, per decoded token for reads
scenes.say: Sparse is the opposite trade. At a million tokens MiniMax keeps more than plain attention would, but each step reads about an eighth.

steps.say: What does reading less cost? With the true top keys, Qwen keeps ninety-eight percent of its long-context score down to five hundred and twelve keys.
Single needles survive. Tasks that need many scattered tokens fail first.

scenes.text: Open models are not dropping global attention. They are putting an indexer, a window or a fixed state in front of it.
scenes.mark: putting an indexer, a window or a fixed state in front of it
scenes.say: Open models are not dropping global attention. They are putting an indexer, a window or a fixed state in front of it.

recap: The chart is Raschka's gallery, reproduced exactly
A wider list: 14.3% still all full
No full attention usually means an indexer
scenes.say: To recap. The chart reproduces from the configs. Full attention survives in small models. And no full attention usually means an indexer.
